scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a configuration change on router8, router7 reports that its
OSPF adjacency with router8 dropped (neighbor went INIT/DOWN, then
gone) and some Campus 2 routes flapped. Campus-1-to-Campus-1
traffic still works and Campus 2 PCs reach their local SVI. Find
what broke the router7<->router8 adjacency.

injection.action: change OSPF area for the 172.25.1.0 network to a
injection.command:
vtysh -c "configure terminal" \
        -c "router ospf" \
        -c "no network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0" \
        -c "network 172.25.1.0/24 area 7" \
        -c "exit" -c "exit"
  vtysh -c "clear ip ospf process"

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router8 OSPF area configuration on the
  172.25.1.0/24 link
Mechanism: OSPF requires both ends of an adjacency to agree
  on the area ID. router7's eth5 is 172.25.1.1 in area 0;
  router8's eth4 was 172.25.1.2 in area 0 and was just changed
  to area 7. The hellos now carry mismatched area IDs, so the
  router7<->router8 adjacency drops (Full -> Init -> gone).
  router8 remains in OSPF via its OTHER area-0 links, so traffic
  reroutes and Campus 1 stays mostly reachable -- the observable,
  diagnosable fault is the dropped adjacency on the 172.25.1.0/24
  link, not a full Campus-2 outage.
Localization: router8
Root cause: OSPF area mismatch on the router7<->router8 link
  (router8 in area 7, router7 in area 0)
Fix: on router8 — `vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "no network
  172.25.1.0/24 area 7" -c "network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0"`
scenario.fix_spec:
on router8 — `vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "no network
  172.25.1.0/24 area 7" -c "network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0"`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: OSPF area assignment / area mismatch

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: OSPF process/area assignment on router8 for the inter-router link to router7.

Mechanism: OSPF neighbors must share the same area on a shared network. After the change, router8 started advertising/processing hellos on 172.25.1.0/24 in area 7, while router7 continues to run OSPF area 0 on that same segment. Hellos received with a mismatched Area ID are discarded, so the neighbor briefly appears INIT/DOWN and never forms 2-Way/Full adjacency. With the adjacency gone, LSAs for Campus 2 behind router8 were withdrawn and then reintroduced via other paths, causing the observed route flaps. Local SVIs remained reachable, and Campus 1 internal traffic was unaffected.

Localization: The broken adjacency is on the 172.25.1.0/24 link between router7.eth5 (172.25.1.1) and router8.eth4 (172.25.1.2). Direct evidence:
- router7: “show ip ospf interface eth5” shows Area 0.0.0.0, Neighbor Count 0; “show ip ospf neighbor” has no neighbor on eth5.
- router8: “show ip ospf interface eth4” shows Area 0.0.0.7; “show ip ospf neighbor” has no neighbor on eth4. Running-config confirms “network 172.25.1.0/24 area 7” on router8, while router7 has “network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0”.

Root cause: An incorrect OSPF area change moved 172.25.1.0/24 on router8 into area 7, creating an area mismatch with router7’s area 0.

Corrective fix: Revert router8’s 172.25.1.0/24 interface to area 0 (backbone), e.g. in FRR:
router ospf
 no network 172.25.1.0/24 area 7
 network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0
This will restore the router7–router8 adjacency and stabilize Campus 2 routes.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly localizes the fault to router8 (OSPF area misconfiguration on the 172.25.1.0/24 link).

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: OSPF area assignment / area mismatch
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies an OSPF area assignment mismatch on router8 (172.25.1.0/24 in area 7 vs router7 in area 0) as the root cause.
Agent explicitly identifies the affected link as the 172.25.1.0/24 connection between router7 (eth5 172.25.1.1) and router8 (eth4 172.25.1.2).

The agent explicitly explains that an OSPF area ID mismatch causes hellos to be rejected (preventing 2‑Way/Full adjacency), leading to LSA withdrawal and rerouting while local SVI reachability remains—covering the mechanism clearly.
Recommends removing the network from area 7 and re-adding it to area 0 on router8 (using 'no network ... area 7' and 'network ... area 0'), which exactly matches the expected fix.

The investigation log contains the key observations (running-config and per-interface OSPF area on both routers, and absence of the adjacency in neighbor lists) that support the agent's conclusion that router8's 172.25.1.0/24 was moved to area 7 causing the adjacency to drop. The writeup's inferences follow directly and the recommended fix matches the misconfiguration found.
